name: CASEY CHAN BLDG E2
address: 62968 OB RILEY ROAD BLDG E2, BEND, OR 97701

fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the primary driveway entrance with visible posts or reflective delineators to distinguish it from adjacent vegetation.
• Trim dense vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back any vegetation that reduces sightlines at the driveway entrance onto the public road.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency apparatus to reach both detached structures.
• Mark a designated turnaround area within the property so responding vehicles are not forced to back out onto the road.
• Create and maintain a clear walking path between the main residence and each detached structure for responder movement on foot.
• Trim dense vegetation at the rear of the property to allow responders to approach the back of the structures on foot.
• Keep any gate or barrier on the access drive unlocked or equipped with a Knox-style lock box so responders are not delayed at entry.
• Post a simple site diagram near the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures, the access drive, and any dead ends.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris, fallen branches, and dead plant material from around the base of structures.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Trim branches on scattered trees that hang directly over or within a few feet of any structure.
• Cut back shrubs that are growing against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Mow or cut down grass between the tree clusters and the structure before it dries out seasonally.
• Separate the mixed vegetation growing close to the structure by removing the plants nearest to the walls first.
• Clear woody debris and loose dead material from beneath shrubs near the structure.
• Thin scattered shrubs in the open terrain around the structure so they are not growing in continuous patches.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and debris along its full length.
• Remove any woody debris or dead material that has collected along the edges of the driveway or access route.
• Trim low branches on trees along the access route so vehicles and emergency responders can move through without obstruction.
• Keep grass along the access route cut short to reduce the amount of dry material that could carry fire toward the structure.
